title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between self-concept and self-esteem?
questions.memo:
✓ Self-concept is the picture/beliefs you have about yourself (1)
✓ Self-esteem is how much you value and like yourself (1)

questions.prompt: Which is most likely to LOWER a teenager's self-esteem?
options: Comparing themselves with edited social media photos

questions.prompt: Having healthy self-esteem means thinking you are better than everyone else.
In a SMART goal, what does the T stand for?
Classify each behaviour.

pairs.left: Tries new things without fear of mistakes
Gives in to pressure to be accepted

questions.prompt: Rewrite this negative self-talk as positive self-talk: 'I'm terrible at sport, so there's no point trying.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ Any positive, realistic rewrite, e.g. 'I'm still learning; if I practise, I will improve and enjoy it more.' (2)

questions.prompt: Suggest THREE ways a learner can build healthy self-esteem.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): know your strengths; set realistic goals; positive self-talk; accept mistakes; supportive friends; exercise and sleep; limit comparison; help others

questions.prompt: What is the influence of people your own age on your behaviour called?
Which is an example of POSITIVE peer pressure?
options: Friends encouraging you to join the debating club

questions.prompt: Which response is assertive?
options: 'No thanks, I don't want to. Let's do something else.'
Saying nothing and leaving with them

questions.prompt: What is the free Childline number in South Africa?
Match each communication style to its description.

pairs.right: Gives in and ignores own needs

questions.prompt: Sharing a private photo of someone without their permission can be a form of cyberbullying.
What can a bystander do when they see someone being bullied?
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): don't join in or laugh; support the victim; tell a trusted adult/report it; encourage others to stand up

questions.prompt: Give TWO warning signs of an unhealthy relationship.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): jealousy/control; pressure or threats; name-calling; isolation from friends; dishonesty; violence

questions.prompt: Which change happens in boys during puberty?
What is choosing not to have sex called?
What is the legal age of consent for sexual activity in South Africa?
Explain THREE important things about consent.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): must be freely given without pressure; can be withdrawn at any time; must be clear; cannot be given when drunk, drugged or asleep; age of consent is 16

questions.prompt: Classify each change during puberty.
Name TWO ways in which HIV is spread.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): unprotected sex; sharing needles; infected blood; mother to baby during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding

questions.prompt: What is it called when a person needs more and more of a substance to get the same effect?
Which addictive substance is found in cigarettes and most vapes?
Name the South African organisation that helps people with alcohol and drug dependence. (abbreviation)
Match each substance to one effect.
Describe THREE ways a person's substance abuse can affect their family.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): conflict; broken trust; financial problems; theft; neglect/abuse; emotional stress

questions.prompt: Suggest TWO healthy alternatives to substance use for dealing with stress.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): sport/exercise; talking to someone; hobbies (music, art); youth groups; relaxation; volunteering
